Definition: from G1223 and G4687; to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute in foreign lands:--scatter abroad.
BiblicalUsage: To scatter abroad is what persecution did to the church in Jerusalem, and the scattering became sowing. After Stephen's death the disciples are scattered through Judea and Samaria, and those who are scattered preach the word wherever they go.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the scattering after Stephen is the church's first missionary journey. It was meant to destroy them, and instead it planted the gospel in every town they fled to.
